scope: Long-term product shape for Nara as a mature standalone game editor
authority_note: This file is research evidence, not implementation authority. The recommendation requires focused Accepted ADRs before production work. In particular, child-process Play remains owned by OQ-039, unavailable-schema authoring remains Proposed in ADR 0090, and Product Package and Editor Contribution trust remain owned by OQ-031.

repository_baseline.architecture_overview: Nara already has a real standalone nara-editor executable, a Host-owned Editor workspace, UI-neutral tooling models and typed actions, strict Scene and Prefab document authority, a runtime-independent component schema catalog type, isolated Runtime generations, an in-process embedded Game View, and first-party Scene and UI Prefab authoring. The current product is not yet project-generic for arbitrary Rust code: EditorProjectIntent carries a compiled ProductRecipe, the Reference Game proves project-specific behavior through a compiled editor canary, the Editor open path requires a complete frozen native registry, and the generic editor deliberately does not discover or load arbitrary project Rust code.

module_map.interface: EditorLaunchOptions plus immutable EditorFrameModel consumption and ordered EditorActionBatch submission
module_map.seam: Between the native window, egui and WGPU Adapter implementation and the renderer-neutral Editor project session
module_map.depth: High: one small interface hides window, event-loop, GPU, viewport, input and frame-transaction implementation
module_map.leverage: The same Host-owned authoring workflow can be presented by another toolkit Adapter without changing document or persistence semantics
module_map.locality: Native presentation and toolkit state remain in editor/ and nara_tooling_egui rather than spreading into runtime and document Modules

module_map.interface: Open one project, publish immutable frames, dispatch typed actions, drive authoring and Play, and expose private preview candidates
module_map.seam: Between Host-owned project, document, content and Runtime authority and all Editor presentation Adapters
module_map.depth: Externally deep, but its implementation currently concentrates workspace, persistence, content refresh, preview, UI authoring, Play and Game View coordination in one large owner. Long-term work should preserve the small external interface while deepening private internal Modules rather than widening the public interface.
module_map.leverage: One session enforces exact document revision, save receipt, content generation, Runtime generation and presentation authority across the complete authoring loop
module_map.locality: Correctness is centralized, although future external Play and extensions need private sub-Modules to keep failure and protocol logic local

module_map.interface: Workspace models, selection, Inspector models, commands, Scene and Prefab transactions, Play views and bounded observations
module_map.seam: Between Editor product semantics and toolkit-specific presentation
module_map.depth: High for current Scene and Prefab workflows: adapters learn immutable models and typed commands rather than mutation internals
module_map.leverage: The existing action vocabulary is a strong basis for both another local toolkit Adapter and a future process protocol projection
module_map.locality: Undo, dirty state, selection and document mutation remain outside egui and outside Runtime Worlds

module_map.interface: Stable component and field identities, schema versions, aliases, value kinds, defaults, capabilities, tombstones, codecs, migrations and frozen native bindings
module_map.seam: Between persistent authoring semantics and executable Rust or Bevy binding authority
module_map.depth: The catalog is a promising deep data Module, but the current Editor still reaches it through compiled schema providers and a complete native registry; the ledger explicitly says a non-executable authoring catalog is absent
module_map.leverage: Stable IDs already support Scene, Prefab, patch, Inspector, migration, asset-reference traversal and Runtime verification
module_map.locality: Persistent identity is separated from Rust TypeId, Bevy ComponentId and codec closures, allowing a future standalone authoring bundle without replacing the runtime registry

module_map.interface: Pure, inspectable, replayable compiled Rust product composition with SchemaContribution
module_map.seam: Between project or game code and Host-owned Runtime plan construction
module_map.depth: High for already-compiled trusted Runtime composition; it deliberately does not solve package installation, dynamic discovery, missing-package recovery or Editor contribution hosting
module_map.leverage: One recipe is reused by direct App, headless, desktop and compiled Editor paths
module_map.locality: Plugin and schema composition remain in game or package Rust code instead of being duplicated in nara.toml

module_map.interface: Prepare, publish, drive, pause, step, fault, stop and finitely retire one isolated App generation
module_map.seam: Between executable Host authority and one game Runtime generation
module_map.depth: High and reusable across in-process and child-process deployment because lifecycle semantics do not require transport types
module_map.leverage: The existing Runtime state machine can remain inside a future child game process while the Editor sees a smaller control and observation protocol
module_map.locality: World, schedules, tasks, services, faults and close obligations remain inside the Runtime owner rather than leaking into tooling

implemented_strengths: The Editor Shell is already a separate executable and private first-party application rather than an ECS plugin.
The Host is the sole authority for workspace, persistence, Play and native presentation; Runtime Worlds contain no Editor workspace copy.
Scene and Prefab source documents, stable identities, exact revisions, typed patches, Undo and receipt-backed Save are implemented.
Scene View, Game View and UI Canvas use exact presentation and input receipts instead of treating a rendered image as mutation authority.
The component schema catalog is persistable and excludes Rust TypeId, Bevy ComponentId, function pointers and native handles.
Runtime generations are isolated, restartable and finite-close aware; in-process and child-process placement are explicitly allowed as Host Adapter choices.
ProductRecipe keeps compiled Rust product composition coherent across direct, headless, desktop and compiled Editor paths.
First-party UI authoring is source-based and does not serialize a synthetic Scene or toolkit-owned widget tree.
critical_gaps: The generic editor cannot obtain arbitrary project schema and authoring metadata without compiled project contribution code; the implementation ledger says a non-executable authoring catalog is absent.
Unavailable schema and lossless degraded authoring are still Proposed in ADR 0090 and not implemented; current opening remains complete-schema-only and fail-closed.
The selected Game View is an in-process first placement. Child-process Play, local transport and remote observation remain open under OQ-039 and OQ-041.

The only broad project extension mechanism is compiled Rust ProductRecipe and SchemaContribution. Project packages, Editor contributions, trust tiers and isolated Extension Hosts remain open under OQ-031 and OQ-045.
Animation has no concrete Module or authoring workflow; Material2dDescriptor is intentionally small; reusable shader and material specialization remains open.
Image import is a concrete domain-owned Module, not a general importer contribution system; durable artifact-store workflow and additional asset domains remain incomplete.
The current Reference Game proves a project-compiled Editor companion pattern through a private canary, but that pattern cannot be the recovery editor when project code fails to compile.

candidate_architectures.name: Standalone schema-first editor with external game process
candidate_architectures.overall_verdict: Best mandatory product foundation. It gives the strongest standalone identity, authoring availability and crash isolation, but by itself is too weak for arbitrary executable custom inspectors, windows, gizmos and importers.

module_design.interface: Open or close a project, render immutable Editor frames and submit ordered actions
module_design.implementation_hidden: Project browser, docking, native windows, egui or future toolkit, WGPU, layout persistence and recovery mode

module_design.interface: Open source documents and assets against one immutable Authoring Schema Bundle; expose document sessions, diagnostics and safe operations
module_design.implementation_hidden: Project scan, asset index, schema composition, migration, degraded-record preservation, document codecs, Undo, persistence and source-control-safe writes

module_design.interface: Versioned non-executable stable identities and semantic metadata sufficient for generic authoring
module_design.implementation_hidden: Rust derive or generator details, predecessor lineage, source fingerprints, tombstones, presentation metadata and validation compilation

module_design.interface: Request one project game or schema build and observe structured progress, diagnostics and immutable candidate artifacts
module_design.implementation_hidden: Cargo invocation, target selection, caching, cancellation, last-good retention and toolchain details

module_design.interface: Start from an immutable Play launch bundle, control Pause, Step, Restart and Stop, receive bounded observations, and close
module_design.implementation_hidden: Child process, local transport, protocol encoding, frame transfer, heartbeat, crash detection and process cleanup

candidate_architectures.seam_assessment: The decisive seam is between non-executable authoring authority and executable project behavior. It maximizes depth because the Editor can exercise a large authoring surface through one stable bundle while game code remains behind a process seam. The existing in-process Runtime and the proposed child-process Runtime would make Play placement a real two-Adapter seam rather than a hypothetical abstraction.

workflow_stress_test.scene_ui_animation_shader: Scene and current UI Prefab authoring fit directly. Animation clips, controllers, material assets, shader source or graphs must become first-party domain documents with their own stable identities, diagnostics, preview compilers and Runtime lowering. They must not be forced into one universal component-field editor.
workflow_stress_test.play_and_run: Play builds only the project game or development-player target, launches a supervised child process and may pass an immutable unsaved Scene or Prefab snapshot through a bounded launch bundle. Run uses the shipping-like project executable and on-disk or exported content. The Editor remains alive through build failure or game crash.
workflow_stress_test.custom_inspectors_windows_gizmos_importe: Built-in tools and declarative schema metadata work well. Arbitrary executable project tools do not; candidate A therefore needs candidate D for mature extension coverage.
workflow_stress_test.missing_schema_or_code: The Editor opens from the last compatible Authoring Schema Bundle or, after ADR 0090-style admission, preserves bounded unknown records in a Degraded document. Unsafe field edits, remaps, Cook and Play fail closed. Broken Rust code does not prevent source recovery.
workflow_stress_test.crash_isolation: Strong. Game panics, unsafe project code and native game libraries retire the child Play session rather than the Editor process. The Editor still needs protection from its own first-party code and any in-process extension tier.
workflow_stress_test.build_and_reload_latency: Data-only edits require no project build. Runtime data reload may update the child when the owning domain permits it. Rust structural changes build a fresh executable candidate and restart only the child. Compatible body hot patching remains optional and must beat rebuild plus restart in measured evidence.
workflow_stress_test.migration_from_current: Moderate. Preserve nara-editor, EditorProjectSession, nara_tooling, document Modules and RuntimeInstance. Add a persisted Authoring Schema Bundle, decouple project open from complete native binding, accept degraded authoring, and implement a child-process Play Adapter under OQ-039. The current in-process Game View remains a valuable second Adapter and low-latency option.

depth_and_locality.depth: Very high at the authoring seam if the bundle is sufficient to drive generic Inspector, validation and document operations without executable callbacks
depth_and_locality.leverage: One bundle serves Scene, Prefab, UI, future asset editors, source validation, AI tools and Runtime handshake
depth_and_locality.locality: Build, game crash, IPC and frame transport bugs stay in Play and build Modules; document correctness stays in AuthoringProject

candidate_architectures.name: Project-compiled editor companion with an in-process recipe
candidate_architectures.overall_verdict: Useful opt-in trusted native tier and strong first-party harness; reject as the sole or default standalone-editor architecture.

module_design.interface: Launch the shared Editor implementation with one statically linked ProjectEditorRecipe
module_design.implementation_hidden: Cargo graph, project game crate, Editor-only crate, schema providers, native custom tool Modules and exact build identity

module_design.interface: One immutable compiled composition of Runtime ProductRecipe plus separately typed Editor Module contributions
module_design.implementation_hidden: Dependency ordering, identity checks, preparation, activation and Host-owned shutdown

candidate_architectures.seam_assessment: Static linking avoids a Rust ABI seam and gives excellent direct type leverage, but it moves the project-code seam inside the long-lived Editor process. The external interface can remain small, yet project compilation becomes an availability prerequisite and failures lose locality by taking down the Editor Shell.

workflow_stress_test.scene_ui_animation_shader: Potentially excellent because project Rust can register exact types and bespoke tools. Compilation does not create the missing first-party animation or shader domain models, and current UI structural authoring remains a closed four-kind catalog until a focused successor admits extension.
workflow_stress_test.play_and_run: In-process Play and the current embedded Game View provide the lowest control and frame-transfer overhead. Production Run should still use a separate desktop executable for fidelity and isolation.
workflow_stress_test.custom_inspectors_windows_gizmos_importe: Highest native power. A custom Inspector or gizmo can use typed Rust while still emitting Host-owned actions. Custom windows must not own event loops or workspace state. Importers remain domain Modules rather than a universal registry until multiple workflows prove a shared seam.
workflow_stress_test.missing_schema_or_code: Weakest point. A broken or unavailable project build prevents the newest companion from starting. A cached last-good companion helps but may be stale. A generic recovery editor and independent schema bundle are still required, which means pure candidate B eventually recreates candidate A as a fallback.
workflow_stress_test.crash_isolation: Poor. Project unsafe Rust, native libraries, panic-abort, allocator corruption or Editor Module bugs share the Editor process.
workflow_stress_test.build_and_reload_latency: Initial faithful open requires compiling and linking an Editor companion. Rust changes can rebuild an immutable companion generation, but structural changes require Editor restart and workspace restoration. The editor dependency graph makes link work larger than building the game alone.
workflow_stress_test.migration_from_current: Easy. EditorApplication::open_with_intent, EditorProjectIntent::with_recipe and the Reference Game editor_game_view_canary already demonstrate this pattern. The next step would be a deliberate thin companion crate and ProjectEditorRecipe, but it should remain optional.

depth_and_locality.depth: High for trusted Rust authors because a small recipe unlocks complete native integration
depth_and_locality.leverage: Direct reuse of current ProductRecipe, schema providers, Runtime bridge and typed commands
depth_and_locality.locality: Good compile-time locality but poor failure locality because project code, Editor tools and Shell share one crash domain

candidate_architectures.name: Native dynamic module loading inside the standalone editor
candidate_architectures.overall_verdict: Reject as the default or primary extension architecture. Consider only a future fully trusted, restart-oriented expert tier with a separately admitted stable C-compatible ABI and no requirement for project recovery.

module_design.interface: Load, validate, activate and retire one versioned native module generation through opaque handles
module_design.implementation_hidden: Platform library discovery, symbol resolution, build identity, allocator ownership, callback retirement, thread shutdown, crash markers and restart policy

module_design.interface: C-compatible functions and plain or explicitly encoded records for capability-specific contributions
module_design.implementation_hidden: Rust adapters on both sides; no Rust trait objects, Bevy World, egui values, WGPU handles or Rust-owned allocations cross the seam

candidate_architectures.seam_assessment: A raw Rust cdylib is not a stable seam. Making it safe enough requires a C-compatible ABI, opaque generation handles, allocator and panic rules, and explicit callback retirement. That interface tends to become wide and shallow because every useful Editor behavior must be translated while the module still shares the Editor crash domain.

workflow_stress_test.scene_ui_animation_shader: Native modules can implement any tool, but ordinary source authoring becomes coupled to a successfully built and compatible library unless schema remains separate. If schema is separate, candidate C no longer provides a reason to be the foundational architecture.
workflow_stress_test.play_and_run: Loading project gameplay into the Editor provides low-latency in-process Play but recreates the current shared crash domain and makes safe unloading or state migration difficult. External Run remains necessary.
workflow_stress_test.custom_inspectors_windows_gizmos_importe: Very powerful, including native windows, GPU and import libraries, but those capabilities are exactly where authority leakage and lifecycle bugs become severe. A correct design must deny direct Shell, workspace, WGPU and World access, reducing the supposed advantage.
workflow_stress_test.missing_schema_or_code: A missing, incompatible or unload-failed module removes its types and tools. Recovery mode can suppress native modules, but source safety still requires an independent schema bundle and degraded records.
workflow_stress_test.crash_isolation: Poor. Segmentation faults, ABI mismatch, use-after-unload, foreign threads and native dependencies can crash or corrupt the Editor.
workflow_stress_test.build_and_reload_latency: A project cdylib may link faster than a complete Editor companion, but Windows library locking, static state, thread-local state, callbacks, vtables and Rust layout changes make reliable unload and hot reload expensive. Editor restart is the only honest universal fallback.
workflow_stress_test.migration_from_current: Hard. Nara currently has no dynamic loader, stable native ABI, module generation protocol or unload lifecycle. ProductRecipe and Plugin are Rust-internal interfaces and must not be exported across the ABI.

depth_and_locality.depth: Low unless the ABI becomes so abstract that it resembles the RPC or Wasm protocol from candidate D
depth_and_locality.leverage: High only for trusted native code that needs direct low-level performance
depth_and_locality.locality: Weak because module faults and resource lifetime leak into the Editor process even when the registration interface is narrow

candidate_architectures.name: Hybrid declarative, managed, Wasm and RPC extension architecture
candidate_architectures.overall_verdict: Best mature extension architecture when layered on candidate A. Do not implement it as one universal extension kernel; grow capability-specific Interfaces from concrete Inspector, gizmo, window and importer workflows.

module_design.interface: Versioned schema presentation, validation, menu, action, icon, preview and bounded gizmo descriptors
module_design.implementation_hidden: Generation, package provenance, localization, validation compilation and action lowering

module_design.interface: Activate a versioned extension generation, exchange capability-scoped requests and results, observe health, and retire it
module_design.implementation_hidden: Managed runtime, Wasm engine or native worker process, transport, scheduling, budgets, cancellation, diagnostics, crash recovery and package activation

module_design.interface: Consume a bounded selected-record snapshot and return presentation plus revision-bound typed edit intents
module_design.implementation_hidden: Language runtime, custom validation and UI logic; Host still owns patch, Undo and persistence

module_design.interface: Produce a declarative Nara UI or protocol UI tree and receive semantic actions
module_design.implementation_hidden: Extension state and language toolkit; Editor Shell still owns docking, native windows, focus and input

module_design.interface: Consume selection and viewport facts, return batched primitives and hit proxies, then lower gestures into typed authoring intents
module_design.implementation_hidden: Extension-specific tool state; Host owns camera, picking, capture, transactions and stale-revision rejection

module_design.interface: Consume capability-scoped source bytes and declared settings; return content-addressed artifacts, dependencies and diagnostics
module_design.implementation_hidden: Third-party codecs, native libraries, worker lifetime, caches and cancellation; the Editor asset owner commits results

candidate_architectures.seam_assessment: Candidate D places executable customization behind a replaceable Extension Host seam while the long-lived Editor retains documents, selection, Undo, persistence, windows, GPU and package transactions. Wasm and process RPC are genuinely different Adapters, so a shared lifecycle and contribution protocol can be real, but each domain Interface must remain capability-specific to preserve depth and locality.

workflow_stress_test.scene_ui_animation_shader: First-party domain editors remain native Editor Modules. Extensions can add property presentation, graph nodes, animation tracks, validators and compile operations without becoming document authority. Shader compilation and animation evaluation should run as explicit jobs with last-good artifacts and structured diagnostics.
workflow_stress_test.play_and_run: Uses candidate A's external game process. Managed or Wasm gameplay adapters may have their own Runtime module generations, but Editor extensions and Play Runtime generations remain separate. A failed extension does not restart the game unless it changed Runtime composition.
workflow_stress_test.custom_inspectors_windows_gizmos_importe: Strongest balanced coverage. Declarative metadata handles common Inspectors. Wasm handles portable deterministic tool logic with enforced memory, fuel and capability limits. Managed or native process RPC handles complex windows, importers and domain tools. High-frequency gizmos require batching and retained logical handles rather than chatty per-primitive RPC.
workflow_stress_test.missing_schema_or_code: The schema bundle remains independent. If an executable extension is missing, crashes or has a protocol mismatch, its advanced UI is disabled while source records remain visible and losslessly preserved. A recovery launch can suppress all executable extensions.
workflow_stress_test.crash_isolation: Strong for process-hosted extensions and potentially strong for Wasm only when memory, imports, fuel, time, output and termination are actually enforced. A trusted same-process managed or native optimization must be labelled non-sandboxed and remain optional.
workflow_stress_test.build_and_reload_latency: Extensions build and activate independently from the game and Editor. An Extension Host generation can be replaced without relinking nara-editor. Protocol or state incompatibility falls back to host replacement or Editor restart rather than unsafe in-place mutation.
workflow_stress_test.migration_from_current: Moderate to hard, but incremental. Current immutable frames and typed actions are good semantic source material; they should be projected into versioned protocol records rather than serialized wholesale. Start with declarative Inspector metadata, then one out-of-process importer or tool, then a Wasm or managed Adapter only after a real workflow proves its need.

depth_and_locality.depth: High if each capability Interface hides language runtime, transport and package details while exposing only domain semantics
depth_and_locality.leverage: One Extension Host lifecycle supports multiple languages and failure models; each contribution Interface serves many packages without exposing Editor internals
depth_and_locality.locality: Extension crashes, budgets and reload live in ExtensionHost; document transactions live in AuthoringProject; native window and GPU authority stay in Editor Shell

primary_editor_entry.summary: The mature product should be one installed, project-generic nara-editor application. Project-specific compilation may produce a game executable, schema bundle or optional extension artifact, but must not be required merely to launch the Editor and inspect ordinary source documents.

candidate_comparison.assessment: Excellent. nara-editor opens the project from data and a non-executable schema bundle; project build begins only for schema refresh, code change or Play.
Poor as the default. Users launch a project-specific companion generation; a valid cached generation can be fast, but first faithful open and recovery depend on project compilation.
Superficially generic, but faithful open still depends on a compatible native project module unless schema is separate.
Excellent when layered on A. The Editor stays generic while optional extension generations activate separately.

primary_editor_entry.recommendation: Adopt A as the mandatory entry model and D as the extension model. Keep B as an explicit expert or first-party companion, never the recovery path.

first_open_and_iteration.summary: First open should be project discovery, source indexing, schema validation and import reconciliation, not an Editor build. Iteration should classify data, schema, Rust body, Rust structural and extension changes separately, retain last-good artifacts, and keep the Editor open through failure.

candidate_comparison.assessment: Best zero-build opening and clear data-versus-code iteration. Requires schema bundle generation, stale status and external build orchestration.
Simple trusted implementation but couples availability to Cargo and relinking. Last-good companion plus restart is mandatory.
Can shorten rebuild scope, but loader and unload safety dominate iteration reliability.
Separates Editor, game and extension build loops. Best long-term responsiveness, with protocol and activation complexity.

recommended_iteration_classes: Scene, Prefab, UI, animation, material, shader settings and ordinary asset edits: no Rust build; domain reload or preview compilation with last-good output.
Authoring schema metadata change: rebuild or regenerate only the schema bundle, validate atomically, then adopt a new schema generation.
Compatible Rust body change: optional hot patch only after measured evidence; otherwise incremental game build and child restart.
Structural Rust, dependency, feature or plugin change: fresh game executable and fresh Runtime process.
Editor extension change: replace only the relevant Extension Host generation; preserve Editor workspace and source documents.
Editor Shell or first-party native Module change: rebuild or restart the Editor itself.

authoring_coverage.summary: A mature Nara Editor must host multiple deep domain Modules in one Shell: Scene and Prefab, UI, Animation, Material and Shader, Asset, Inspector, Game and Debug. Shared workspace, selection, transactions, diagnostics and asset identity provide leverage, while each domain keeps its own persistent model and lowering semantics for locality.

current_coverage.scene_and_prefab: Implemented through stable Scene and Prefab documents, exact revisions, patches, Undo, Save, preview and picking.
current_coverage.ui: Implemented for first-party UI Prefab authoring, Canvas preview and a closed Container, Text, Image and Button structural catalog.
current_coverage.animation: Not started as a concrete Module; ADR 0029 only preserves future ownership and stable-target constraints.
current_coverage.material_and_shader: Material2dDescriptor is a small inline data contract; reusable material assets, custom shader interfaces and graph authoring remain open.
current_coverage.assets_and_import: Stable asset metadata and one concrete ImageImporter exist; a durable general artifact-store product and third-party importer contributions do not.
current_coverage.debugging: Play controls, Runtime edits, Apply Changes and bounded observations exist in-process; remote timeline, profiler and reconnectable observation sessions remain open.

candidate_comparison.assessment: Strong for all first-party and data-described authoring; insufficient alone for arbitrary executable project tools.
Maximum native customization but compile-gated and crash-coupled.
Maximum native customization with additional ABI and unload hazards.
Best scalable extension coverage if custom tools use capability-specific protocols rather than Editor internals.

authoring_coverage.recommendation: Build Animation and Material or Shader as first-party data-authoring Modules on A, then use D for project-specific tools. Do not make project code the schema or document parser for those domains.

persistent_data_model.summary: Use authored source documents plus a versioned non-executable Authoring Schema Bundle as durable authority. Keep imported artifacts, shader binaries, thumbnails, preview frames, Runtime lowering and extension caches derived and rebuildable. Separate document format, schema owner lineage, composed schema fingerprint, Runtime build identity, extension protocol and artifact version.
recommended_records: SceneDocument and PrefabDocument with stable entity, component and field identities
UI Prefab and future structured asset documents with domain-owned schemas
Animation clip, controller or timeline documents with domain-owned stable target identities
Material and shader source or graph documents plus declared parameter and binding schemas
Authoring Schema Bundle containing stable type and field IDs, versions, tombstones, aliases, value kinds, defaults, semantic constraints, reference kinds and separately classified presentation hints
Project asset index with stable IDs, source digests, importer identity and dependency facts
Derived artifact records keyed by source, settings, importer and target fingerprints
Editor workspace and layout state kept separate from project Runtime data
Extension manifests and protocol compatibility metadata kept separate from persistent game schemas

candidate_comparison.assessment: Best separation of source, schema, bindings and artifacts.
Can use the same model, but tends to treat compiled Rust as schema availability authority.
Risks making a loaded module the type and migration authority.
Preserves A and adds versioned extension contribution data without making extension memory durable.

guardrails: Do not serialize Rust TypeId, Bevy Entity or ComponentId, function pointers, trait objects, VM handles, native paths, GPU handles or toolkit objects.
Do not turn the component catalog into a universal object system for assets, animation, shaders and extension UI; each domain owns its model.
Do not let a missing extension imply that its persistent records were deleted.
Do not use derived cache presence as source authority or uninstall ownership.

project_code_loading.summary: The default Editor process should load no arbitrary project Rust code. Project Runtime code belongs in the game process. Executable Editor customization belongs in an isolated Extension Host or, exceptionally, a fully trusted static companion. Arbitrary Rust cdylib loading is rejected as the normal seam.

candidate_comparison.loading_model: No project code in Editor; game executable runs out of process
Statically linked project and Editor companion
Native dynamic library loaded in Editor
Declarative data in Editor; managed, Wasm or native code in replaceable Extension Hosts

interface_rules: ProductRecipe remains the compiled Runtime composition Interface and is owned by the game executable; it must not become a language-neutral Editor extension kernel.
The Editor consumes a non-executable product and schema description with exact fingerprints, not Rust plugin objects.
No process seam carries Rust trait objects, Bevy World or Entity, egui values, WGPU handles or Rust-owned allocations.
Every executable extension declares trust, capabilities, budgets, cancellation, persistent-state policy, failure scope and restart behavior.
A same-process managed or native optimization is fully trusted and non-sandboxed, and must retain Editor restart fallback.

play_execution_model.summary: Make external supervised Play the mature default while retaining the current in-process Game View as a second Adapter and optional low-latency mode. Both placements preserve one Runtime lifecycle and tooling semantics; transport remains private to the concrete Adapter.
recommended_flow: Editor captures an immutable PlayLaunchBundle containing project, profile, document or unsaved snapshot, schema fingerprint, content revision and expected game build identity.
GameBuildOrchestrator produces or selects a last-good project development-player executable and structured build result.
Editor starts a child process with a private versioned local connection and performs an exact handshake before granting Runtime observation, frame or input authority.
The child constructs the existing RuntimeInstance and ProductRecipe inside its own process, then reports generation-stamped state and diagnostics.
Play, Pause, exact Step, Runtime edit and Apply Changes use bounded semantic commands and results; the document remains the authoring authority.
External window is the first reliable presentation. Embedded Game View later transports frames and input without removing the process seam.
Stop or crash retires the child and all generation-scoped handles. Restart uses a fresh process and Runtime generation.
Run launches the shipping-like desktop executable against saved or exported content and does not consume unsaved Editor state by default.

candidate_comparison.assessment: Best crash isolation and honest rebuild semantics; adds IPC and frame-transport work.
Best latency and direct integration; weakest failure isolation.
Similar latency to B with additional unsafe reload complexity.
Uses A for game execution and keeps Editor extension failures separate from Runtime failures.

play_execution_model.architecture_compatibility: This recommendation preserves ADR 0082 and ADR 0084 lifecycle semantics but changes the preferred deployment Adapter. It requires a focused OQ-039 decision and must not silently rewrite ADR 0112's currently accepted bounded in-process placement.

editor_extension_model.summary: Use a graded extension ladder. First-party domain editors remain internal Modules. Common project customization is declarative. Executable customization runs in a replaceable Extension Host through capability-specific Interfaces. A static native companion is optional; native dynamic loading is not the default.

extension_ladder.name: Wasm guest
extension_ladder.failure_scope: Guest instance when memory, imports, fuel, time, output and termination are enforced

extension_ladder.name: Managed or native process Extension Host
uses: Complex docked windows through declarative UI

extension_ladder.name: Static trusted ProjectEditorCompanion
uses: First-party or expert tools that cannot meet latency or authority needs through isolation
extension_ladder.failure_scope: Entire Editor process; explicit trust and restart required

capability_interfaces.custom_inspector: Snapshot in, declarative presentation and typed edit intents out; Host applies patch and Undo.
capability_interfaces.custom_window: Declarative Nara UI or protocol UI tree plus semantic actions; Editor Shell owns docking, focus, native windows and persistence.
capability_interfaces.gizmo: Batched primitives and hit proxies plus gesture intents; Host owns camera, input capture, picking, transaction and stale rejection.
capability_interfaces.importer: Capability-scoped source and settings in; artifact manifest, dependencies and diagnostics out; asset owner commits or rejects.
capability_interfaces.animation_or_shader_extension: Domain-owned node, track or compiler contribution records; no arbitrary mutation of document internals or GPU state.

seam_discipline: Do not introduce one universal extension Interface before concrete Inspector, gizmo, window and importer consumers prove common lifecycle needs.

One Adapter is hypothetical. The first executable extension can remain a concrete process Module; promote a shared ExtensionHost seam only when a second Adapter such as Wasm or managed hosting exists.
Tests cross the same semantic Interface as production extensions and use in-memory or local process Adapters rather than privileged internal hooks.
The deletion test must pass: removing ExtensionHost should force lifecycle, version, budget and crash handling back into every extension, proving that the Module earns its depth.

failure_and_versioning_model.summary: Keep the Editor and authored source available through project code, game and extension failure. Version every authority independently, retain last-good artifacts, make recovery mode explicit, and never interpret missing code as deletion authority.
version_axes: Project manifest and document format versions
Schema owner lineage and composed Authoring Schema Bundle fingerprint
Native Runtime executable build identity and ProductRecipe composition identity
Play local-protocol version and Runtime generation
Extension package identity, Extension Host protocol and extension generation
Importer identity, settings fingerprint and artifact format version
Shader compiler and target artifact identity
missing_schema_policy: Recognized document and generic value grammar plus unavailable schema enters Degraded authoring only after ADR 0090-style evidence is accepted.
Preserve complete bounded semantic records and stable references; do not fabricate ECS placeholder bindings.
Allow metadata inspection, canonical save without touching unavailable records and proven unrelated edits.
Reject field edits, unknown-reference remaps, prefab overrides, Cook, export and Play that require unavailable semantics.
A compatible recovered schema or extension reclassifies the document through a new generation; source rewrite remains explicit.

failure_matrix.behavior: Editor and current documents remain live; last-good schema and game candidate remain identified; Play start reports structured failure.
Play session becomes faulted or disconnected, all generation handles retire, Editor authoring continues.
Disable or replace that extension generation, preserve documents and first-party tools, offer recovery launch.
Retire the guest request or generation, report bounded diagnostics, do not mutate Host state.
Reject activation before granting mutation, input, frame or persistence authority.
Retain last-good artifact and source authority; diagnostics identify the failed generation and inputs.

failure_matrix.failure: Native companion or native dynamic extension crash
failure_matrix.behavior: Process crash marker and safe next launch; generic recovery editor remains available.

strengths.summary: The recommended A plus D shape preserves Nara's strongest existing Modules while making the product genuinely standalone and resilient.
items: One recognizable Editor application opens projects without compiling a bespoke Editor.
The authoring schema seam provides high leverage across Scene, Prefab, UI, future domain assets, AI tools and validation.
Game and executable extension faults have process or guest locality instead of taking down document authority.
Data edits avoid Rust builds; code and extension builds are classified and independently replaceable.
Current Host-owned workspace, typed actions, receipt-backed persistence and Runtime lifecycle remain reusable rather than rewritten.
ProductRecipe stays a deep compiled Runtime composition Module instead of becoming a universal package or Editor kernel.
Capability-specific extension Interfaces preserve domain semantics and prevent egui, WGPU, World and native handles from becoming ecosystem contracts.
The model scales from artists and designers using data tools to expert Rust developers using an optional static companion.

weaknesses.summary: The recommended shape has higher initial systems cost than simply compiling project code into the Editor, and it creates protocol and artifact responsibilities that must remain tightly scoped.
items: A non-executable authoring bundle must be sufficiently expressive without becoming a universal object system or a second Rust compiler frontend.
External Play requires build orchestration, process supervision, versioned handshake, bounded observations and eventually frame or input transport.
Lossless degraded authoring requires careful operation gates, reference barriers and migration evidence.
Extension Hosts require package trust, lifecycle, budgets, cancellation, protocol compatibility, UI contribution and crash-recovery product design.
High-frequency gizmos, profilers and live scene observation can suffer RPC overhead unless requests are batched and generation-scoped.
A Wasm label is not enough to claim sandboxing; target-specific enforcement and reclamation tests are required.
Supporting both in-process and child-process Play creates two placement Adapters and parity tests.
Keeping a static companion tier increases documentation and support surface even if it is not the default.

nara_transferable_lessons.summary: Copy the mature engines' standalone product shape, data and cache separation, recovery and specialized domain editors; adapt their reflection and extension mechanisms to Rust; reject compile-to-view and unrestricted in-process native loading as the default.
copy: Godot's one generic Editor, source-versus-import cache separation, missing-type preservation, recovery mode and separate Play process.
Unity's stable asset identity, source and artifact databases, Safe Mode, generic serialized property transactions, domain reload classification and out-of-process import workers.
Unreal's family of domain editors, queryable asset metadata, explicit Play or Simulate or Standalone distinctions, extension ladder and derived-data separation.
Fyrox's command-based Editor internals, broad Rust-native authoring coverage and supervised child-process Play.
Nara's existing Host-owned workspace, exact revisions, typed actions, stable schema IDs, isolated Runtime generations and exact presentation receipts.
adapt: Replace load-code-to-discover-schema with a versioned non-executable Authoring Schema Bundle generated from Rust declarations or trusted package metadata.
Keep a last-good bundle bound to source and composition fingerprints; stale schema is visible and cannot impersonate the running game.
Project gameplay runs in a child process by default, while the current in-process bridge becomes an optional placement Adapter.
Custom Inspectors integrate through the same typed patch and Undo path as first-party tools, not through direct document or World mutation.
Advanced tools use Wasm or supervised process RPC; a static native companion remains an explicit trusted tier.
Animation and shader tools are domain Modules with their own source, compile and preview contracts rather than generic component reflection callbacks.
Importers return immutable candidate artifacts and diagnostics; the asset owner retains publication authority.
reject: A project-generated Editor executable as the only way to view or repair source.
Arbitrary Rust cdylib or dyn Plugin loading as the default Editor extension ABI.
A universal UObject-like authority combining persistence, Runtime identity, reflection, scripting and Editor state.
Silent deletion or zeroing of unknown component, asset or extension data.
In-process game execution as the only mature Play placement.
A universal importer, graph, behavior or extension kernel created before independent consumers prove a seam.
Toolkit objects, native handles, raw World access or transport types in durable project Interfaces.

minimum_viable_path.summary: The smallest credible path is not the entire hybrid system. First make nara-editor data-complete and recovery-capable, then add external Play, then add one concrete isolated extension workflow before generalizing.

phases.name: Decision and evidence reset
deliverables: Open a focused product decision that explicitly chooses a generic standalone Editor as the primary entry and records B and C as non-default alternatives.
Define measurable first-open, data-edit, Rust-build, child-start, restart and extension-reload latency scenarios without inventing targets before a baseline.
Reconcile ADR 0112 and OQ-039 so the current in-process placement remains valid evidence while child-process Play becomes a deliberate second Adapter.
Admit or reject ADR 0090 through the required missing-provider, missing-binding, migration and future-schema fixtures before claiming recovery authoring.

phases.name: Offline generic project opening
deliverables: Persist a deterministic Authoring Schema Bundle using the existing stable IDs, versions, tombstones and catalog envelope, while keeping native codecs and Runtime bindings out of it.
Make nara-editor open nara.toml, source asset inventory, Scene, Prefab and UI documents from that bundle without a compiled project recipe.
Separate AuthoringProject schema validation from Runtime complete-binding validation.
Implement visible Complete, Stale and, only after acceptance, Degraded states with lossless unknown-record operation gates.
Keep the current compiled ProductRecipe path for Runtime and exact handshake verification.

phases.name: Complete first-party data authoring
deliverables: Finish one coherent Scene, Prefab and UI source workflow through the generic Editor for both starter and Reference Game without a project-specific Editor binary.
Add a project asset index and durable image artifact-cache loop with stable identity, import settings, failure records and last-good artifacts.
Add one concrete Animation Module, preferably a small sprite animation workflow, with timeline, preview, stable targets, save and Runtime consumption.
Add one Material or Shader authoring workflow with source data, compiler job, preview, diagnostics and last-good artifact retention.
Keep these as first-party domain Modules; do not add a universal extension registry yet.

phases.name: External Play Adapter
deliverables: Build only the project game or development-player target through a private build Adapter with structured diagnostics and cancellation.
Launch a supervised child process with exact project, schema, content and build handshake.
Support Play, Pause, exact Step, Stop, Restart, logs and a minimal bounded remote hierarchy or value observation channel.
Use an external game window first. Preserve the existing in-process Game View and prove semantic parity across both Adapters.
Add embedded child-process Game View only after process lifecycle and external presentation are reliable.

phases.name: First isolated Editor extension
deliverables: Choose one real project workflow, preferably a custom Inspector plus validator or a native-codec importer, and implement it in one supervised Extension Host.
Keep workspace, Undo, selection, persistence, native window and GPU authority in the Editor.
Version the contribution protocol, enforce request budgets and cancellation, retain last-good activation, and prove crash recovery.
Do not create a general ExtensionHost Interface until a second Adapter or heterogeneous extension proves shared lifecycle leverage.

phases.name: Hybrid extension ladder
deliverables: Add a Wasm or managed Adapter only when a second concrete tool justifies the common seam.
Add declarative custom windows, gizmos, graph nodes and importer settings through capability-specific Interfaces.
Retain a generated static ProjectEditorCompanion for fully trusted expert or first-party workflows that cannot meet latency needs through isolation.
Keep raw native dynamic loading rejected unless a future measured case justifies a stable C ABI and accepts Editor-process crash scope.

minimum_viable_path.acceptance_trajectory: Install or build nara-editor once; open an unbuilt project with project-defined records; inspect and edit safe Scene, Prefab and UI data; undo, save and reopen; continue authoring when project Rust is broken; edit one animation and one material or shader asset; press Play; build only the game; launch a child Runtime with matching schema and content identity; observe output and diagnostics; pause, step, restart and stop; crash the game and an extension without losing Editor documents; disable executable extensions in recovery mode; reopen the project without compiling a bespoke Editor.
non_goals_for_first_release: Native object reinstancing or universal Rust hot patching
A universal importer or extension kernel
Embedded cross-process Game View before external Play is reliable
Complete animation, cinematic, modeling or shader-graph parity with mature commercial engines
A package marketplace or signing ecosystem before OQ-031 has concrete product evidence

architecture_comparison.scale: 1 is poor and 5 is strong for Nara's target product; complexity scores are reversed, where 5 means lowest added complexity.
architecture_comparison.interpretation: A wins the product foundation. D closes A's extension gap but should be staged because its protocol and package costs are high. B is the simplest path from current code and remains valuable as an opt-in trusted native tier. C has no decisive advantage after a non-executable schema and process extension host exist, while keeping the worst crash and ABI risks.

decisive_recommendation.name: Standalone schema-first Nara Editor with external Play and a staged isolated extension ladder

selected_composition.mature_extension_model: Candidate D, introduced incrementally through concrete capability Interfaces
selected_composition.retained_optional_tier: Candidate B for first-party or fully trusted expert projects

decisive_recommendation.decision: Nara should ship one project-generic nara-editor process that can open, inspect, edit, save and recover source documents from non-executable schemas without building or loading project Rust. The project game should build and run as a supervised child process for mature Play and Run. Custom Editor behavior should first be declarative, then move to Wasm or supervised managed or native Extension Hosts through capability-specific protocols. The existing in-process Runtime and compiled Editor companion remain useful Adapters, not the product identity.
why_this_is_decisive: It matches the convergent mature-engine evidence while addressing Rust's lack of a stable native language ABI.
It preserves Nara's accepted Host, document, schema identity, Runtime lifecycle and typed-action architecture instead of replacing it.
It provides the strongest source recovery, crash isolation and clear iteration classification.
It keeps ProductRecipe deep and local to compiled Runtime composition rather than turning it into a universal package or Editor Interface.
It gives artists and designers a usable editor even when programmers have broken the build.
It still leaves an explicit high-power native path for cases where measured latency or authority needs exceed isolated protocols.
non_negotiable_invariants: Opening authored source never requires compiling a project-specific Editor executable.
Project source data cannot authorize code download, build scripts, native loading or extension activation by itself.
The long-lived Editor owns workspace, document, selection, Undo, persistence, window, GPU and package transactions.
Runtime and extension code never receive unrestricted mutable Editor state or raw persistent storage authority.
Unknown or unavailable schema is never silent deletion authority.
Every Runtime, schema, artifact and extension generation is explicit and stale requests fail closed.
No raw Rust ABI, Bevy World, toolkit object or GPU handle crosses a process or package seam.
A new shared Interface requires at least two real Adapters or independent consumers; first implementations remain concrete Modules.
required_architecture_decisions_before_i: Accept, revise or reject ADR 0090 for degraded lossless authoring.
Resolve OQ-039 for child-process Play and the smallest local connection while preserving ADR 0112 as the first in-process placement.
Resolve the non-executable Authoring Schema Bundle source, storage, owner lineage and freshness contract under ADR 0081, OQ-044 and a focused successor.
Resolve OQ-031 only for the first concrete Editor contribution and trust workflow; do not pre-accept a universal package kernel.
Select one first-party Animation workflow and one Material or Shader workflow before freezing their authoring Interfaces.
Define measurable edit-to-result and recovery scenarios so protocol or companion choices remain evidence-driven.
migration_sequence: Keep nara-editor, EditorProjectSession and nara_tooling as the stable product front and semantic seam.
Introduce AuthoringProject as a private deep Module that opens from a non-executable schema bundle and does not require Runtime native bindings.
Project the existing catalog and ProductRecipe fingerprints into separate authoring and executable identities; do not duplicate composition authority in nara.toml.
Add degraded source preservation after ADR 0090 evidence, then convert the generic starter and Reference Game to open through the same unbuilt Editor path.
Add a child-process Play Adapter that hosts the existing RuntimeInstance and prove parity with the current in-process Adapter.
Add one concrete isolated Editor extension, then promote only proven lifecycle facts into ExtensionHost.
Retain the compiled companion entry for first-party canaries and expert tools, but always provide the generic recovery Editor.

rejected_alternatives.alternative: Make the project-compiled Editor companion the only official editor
rejected_alternatives.reason: It reproduces compile-before-open, prevents reliable recovery from broken project code, broadens the Editor crash domain and makes project switching and Editor distribution project-specific.
rejected_alternatives.pragmatic_retention: Keep as an optional fully trusted tier and first-party conformance harness.

rejected_alternatives.alternative: Load arbitrary Rust cdylibs or dyn Plugin objects into nara-editor
rejected_alternatives.reason: Rust and trait-object ABIs are unstable; allocator, panic, vtable, thread, callback and unload rules are unsafe; native faults share the Editor process; a safe C ABI loses the direct Rust simplicity that motivated the design.
rejected_alternatives.pragmatic_retention: Only a future separately admitted C-compatible expert ABI with opaque handles and Editor restart fallback.

rejected_alternatives.alternative: Keep in-process Play as the only mature placement
rejected_alternatives.reason: It gives excellent latency but cannot isolate unsafe game code or native dependencies from the Editor and makes structural rebuild or crash recovery more expensive.
rejected_alternatives.pragmatic_retention: Keep as a second Adapter and optional low-latency path after semantic parity exists.

rejected_alternatives.alternative: Make Wasm the universal package, gameplay, importer and Editor ABI
rejected_alternatives.reason: Wasm does not define domain semantics, UI, debugger, packaging, state migration or efficient high-frequency access by itself. It would force one mechanism across unrelated workflows.
rejected_alternatives.pragmatic_retention: Use as one ExtensionHost Adapter for concrete portable and enforceably sandboxed tools.

rejected_alternatives.alternative: Build one universal reflection object model for all scenes, assets, animation, shaders, UI and extensions
rejected_alternatives.reason: It would collapse independent domain semantics into a shallow global Interface, conflict with plugin-owned specialized domains and recreate a UObject or ClassDB-style control plane.
rejected_alternatives.pragmatic_retention: Share stable identity, value and transaction primitives only where independent domain consumers prove leverage.

rejected_alternatives.alternative: Use a running game process as the only source of schema for the Editor
rejected_alternatives.reason: It still requires a successful build and Runtime merely to view source, cannot support offline recovery, and makes Runtime state a dependency of authoring availability.
rejected_alternatives.pragmatic_retention: Use Runtime schema and fingerprints as verification and live-inspection evidence, not sole authoring authority.

uncertain: Exact first-open, incremental build, child start, restart, frame transport and extension activation latency must be measured on representative Nara projects; no numeric claim is made.

The exact source and storage path for the Authoring Schema Bundle is undecided. It may be committed source, generated project output or a content-addressed cache, but freshness and owner lineage must be explicit.
The first child-process frame transport is undecided. External window should precede shared textures, video, CPU readback or platform-specific embedding.
The first executable Editor extension language or host is undecided. Wasm, .NET and native process RPC serve different workflows and trust levels.
The extension UI representation is undecided. A Nara UI document, a smaller semantic widget protocol or a domain-specific view model requires a concrete custom-window tracer.
The acceptable latency and authority threshold for retaining a static native companion tier is not yet measured.
Shader and animation document models remain unselected because Nara has no concrete production tracer for either domain.
Undocumented proprietary implementation details in Unity and Unreal are not assumed beyond their public documentation.
This research does not decide package registry, marketplace, signing, collaboration, remote Editor, multiple concurrent Play targets or cross-machine debugging.
